news.title: Notion’s Confusing Credit Model
news.gist: Notion has gone through four AI pricing setups: a paid add-on, AI folded into paid plans, Custom Agents sold on credits, and now two separate credit balances on every Business and Enterprise seat. One balance covers work where Notion picks the model; the other covers work where the user picks the model, plus Custom Agents. The two balances reset monthly, can’t be pooled and don’t roll over, and a third, shared workspace balance can top up either one. Litterst argues Notion should absorb this complexity instead of passing it to customers, for example with one pool or a separate balance only for Custom Agents.

news.title: Baseten cuts Reflection Beam rates 69-72% in a 47-change week
news.gist: PricingSaaS’s weekly review calls 19–25 Oct the quietest week of the quarter, with fewer than a quarter of the usual number of moves. No price increases were logged, and packaging and product updates far outnumbered changes to the price itself. The biggest move was Baseten cutting its new Reflection Beam API rates four days after launch; HubSpot’s free email cut and Pictory’s merged credit pool also made the top list.

news.title: Developer Tool Pricing Report, October 2026
news.gist: AgentDeals’ monthly tally of developer-tool pricing moves, updated through 27 Oct, counts far more changes than in September, and almost every change with a clear direction went against buyers. Most of the negative moves trim free allowances: smaller sign-up credits at Browser Use, tighter free rate limits at Groq, and no more monthly inference credits for free Hugging Face accounts. Paid bills rise without list-price changes too: Modal now meters egress, Fly.io raised its memory rate, and OVHcloud bills storage and IPv4 as separate lines. Meta also resumed charging for WhatsApp service messages beyond a free monthly allowance.

news.why: The free tier you evaluated on may be gone at renewal, and costs creep in through new line items rather than higher list prices. Check egress, storage and per-message fees, not just the headline rate.

news.title: Developer Tool Pricing Changes: October 19–25, 2026
news.gist: AgentDeals’ weekly digest for our week is mostly about retired models: OpenAI ended access to a long list of older models, Google shut down several Gemini previews, and Together AI pulled two models from serverless inference. The two packaging changes that matter most are at Socket.dev, whose Free plan now covers a single developer seat instead of unlimited developers, and HiveMQ, which stopped new Serverless clusters and will retire that plan, free tier included, at year end. Mistral’s launch discount on Mistral Large 4 also ended.

news.why: Retired models and closed free tiers force migrations, and the replacement is usually priced differently. Budget for the move as well as the new rate.

news.title: How to build an AI brain for your positioning
news.gist: A guest post on loading an AI assistant with customer quotes and competitor notes to rework a company’s messaging. It doesn’t discuss pricing.

patterns.p: HubSpot no longer gives Starter its own email-send limit; sends now draw on the same Credits pool as other actions. Cust swapped cost ranges for a fixed credit cost per AI action and started charging credits for Teammates chats. Both changes come from PricingSaaS reports. More of what a plan includes is now stated in credits rather than in features or caps.

HubSpot cut free marketing email sends from 2,000 to 300 a month, while Zoom raised free Basic’s in-meeting AI questions from 3 to 20 and Dropzone AI removed the investigations cap on its base plan. Vendors loosen limits where they want people to try an AI feature and tighten them where the free plan was giving away the core product. HubSpot and Dropzone AI come from PricingSaaS reports; Zoom is our own capture.

patterns.t: Prices published at a finer grain
patterns.p: Avalara replaced a contact-sales bundle table with public prices per state, Intercom now bills WhatsApp per message instead of per conversation, and Day listed its new top plan at a price per agent. Each change ties the bill to a smaller, published unit, which is easier to compare but harder to forecast. Avalara and Day come from PricingSaaS reports; Intercom is our own capture.

stats_analysis.p: Our own captures only started on 24 Oct, so apart from Zoom and Intercom, this week’s changes come from PricingSaaS reports. PricingSaaS itself called it the quietest week of the quarter. Treat the shares below as directional only.

stats_analysis.figNote: changes reshaped plans rather than raising or cutting cost
stats_analysis.p: New tiers at Day and Avalara, fixed credit costs at Cust, a new WhatsApp billing unit at Intercom and Bolt’s feature swap on Pro all repackage the offer without a clear price direction. All but Intercom come from PricingSaaS reports. PricingSaaS’s market-wide review shows the same tilt, with packaging shifts well ahead of price changes.

stats_analysis.figNote: changes that lower vs raise what buyers pay
stats_analysis.p: Baseten’s token-rate cut, Zoom’s larger free AI allowance and Dropzone AI’s uncapped investigations all favor buyers. The only increase was HubSpot’s free-plan email cut, which is a tighter limit, not a list-price rise. Apart from Zoom, all of these come from PricingSaaS reports.

stats_analysis.figNote: changes touch AI features, models or usage
stats_analysis.p: Model prices (Baseten), AI features moving between plans (Bolt, Day), AI allowances (Zoom, Dropzone AI) and credits per AI action (Cust) make up most of the week. Among market leaders, only Zoom’s change involves AI; HubSpot and Intercom changed email and messaging limits.

stats_analysis.figNote: changes from market leaders, one each: up, down and packaging
stats_analysis.p: HubSpot tightened its free plan, Zoom loosened its free plan and Intercom changed a billing unit. Two of the three changes target a free plan, in opposite directions. The leaders show no common direction this week; each moved a different lever.

Krea’s and Runway’s unlimited-generation offers ended, and Synthesia cut its Syren launch credits. The only new offer was Intercom’s $19 Essential seat for new customers, which looks like one arm of a price test. All four come from PricingSaaS reports.

news_trends.t: Credits spread, and get harder to read
news_trends.p: Notion now splits each seat’s AI usage into two credit balances, HubSpot moved Starter email sends onto shared Credits, and Cust gave each AI action a fixed credit price. Credits let vendors add new actions without new price lines, but buyers can’t easily translate them back into what they used to get.

news_trends.t: Free tiers shrink at the edges
news_trends.p: Developer-tool vendors trimmed sign-up credits, free rate limits and free seats through October, and HubSpot cut its free email allowance this week. The counter-moves, such as Zoom’s and Dropzone AI’s, open up one specific feature rather than restoring a generous free plan.

news_trends.t: Even a quiet week is mostly packaging
news_trends.p: In a week with no logged price increases, PricingSaaS still counted packaging shifts at almost four times straight price changes. The cost changes AgentDeals found mostly came as new line items, like egress or storage fees, rather than higher rates. The same goes for our own sample, where HubSpot cut an allowance and Bolt swapped features without changing a sticker price.

news_trends.t: Messaging moves to a per-message meter
news_trends.p: Meta resumed charging for WhatsApp service messages beyond a free monthly allowance, and Intercom’s FAQ now says WhatsApp is charged per message sent rather than per conversation. That Intercom is passing through Meta’s model is our inference; Intercom doesn’t say so.
